subject: Production: intermittent streaming aborts + 5xx/429 surge
messages:
From: Emma Shaw <emma@velocimed.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: eng-oncall@velocimed.com; procurement@velocimed.com
Date: 2027-04-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production: chat sessions aborting, 5xx/429 spike

Aditya —

We started seeing a spike in 5xx/429 responses this morning (~08:50 PT) across a handful of our interactive chat flows. Client-side behavior: sessions abort mid-stream, and our mobile clients are retrying aggressively (15s client timeout). The result is a visible retry loop and a higher error rate for the last 30 minutes.

Impact: roughly 2% of active sessions are failing to complete. Two customers have flagged the issue and one has an upcoming demo at 11:30 PT. This is causing real revenue and trust impact.

Attached: sr-12345-logs.txt and a small heap-dump of retry samples (retry-heap-samples.json). We need immediate help:
- Root cause assessment (5xx vs 429 source)
- Immediate mitigations (workarounds we can apply now)
- ETA for a durable fix

Please escalate as needed — this is high priority for us.

Thanks,
Emma Shaw
VP Product, VelociMed
[Attachment: sr-12345-logs.txt (text/plain), retry-heap-samples.json (application/json)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com; sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: Emma Shaw <emma@velocimed.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: chat sessions aborting, 5xx/429 spike

Marissa / Sean —

Thanks Emma for the signal and logs. Quick triage notes from my initial pass:
- 429s appear concentrated on streaming completion endpoints (chunked responses). The client-side aborts line up with our keepalive/idle timeout boundary at ~15s.
- 5xx patterns show transient "backend unavailable" followed by a burst of retries; likely a combination of upstream LB idle-timeouts and request amplification from client retries.

Immediate action plan (30–120 min window):
1) Increase LB idle timeout & connection keepalive to 60s for VelociMed tenant (temp change) — Marissa, can you push that?
2) Apply server-side per-API throttling for this tenant (token-bucket) to smooth bursts. Sean, can you prepare the throttling policy and a kill-switch?
3) Publish short-running client guidance to VelociMed: increase client-side stream timeout to 45s and add exponential backoff (jitter) on 429s. Emma, asking if we can get a banner to their engineers now.
4) Enable fallback routing to warmed small-model pool for interactive sessions to reduce latency until we stabilize. Ops will need the go-ahead to route.

Ask: I want to loop in Lauren and leadership if this hits >5% or if VelociMed requests credits. For now we will prioritize operational mitigations.

I've attached the logs from Emma to the internal thread and started a live incident Slack channel.

-Aditya
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sr-12345-logs.txt referenced]

Date: 2027-04-20T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation summary & recommended customer outcome (VelociMed)

Team — executive summary for leadership:

What happened
- 2027-04-19 08:50 PT: VelociMed reported increased 5xx and 429s tied to streaming completion endpoints. Client-side timeouts at ~15s caused aborted streams and an amplification of retries.
- Impact: ~2% of active sessions (initially), customer reported demo risk and revenue exposure.
- Root cause (interim): combination of LB/keepalive timeout mismatch + client aggressive retry behavior; secondary effect was transient backend overload during the retry surge.

Actions taken
- LB idle timeout raised to 60s for the VelociMed tenant (temporary config) — completed 2027-04-19 09:50 PT.
- Tenant-scoped throttling (token-bucket) applied; kill-switch available.
- Advised VelociMed to increase client timeout and add exponential backoff (they confirmed).
- Traffic routed to warmed small-model pool for interactive sessions; latency improved and 5xx/429 rates dropped noticeably.

Current status (as of 2027-04-20 15:45 PT)
- Error rate returned to baseline for VelociMed. Customer confirms stabilization and is monitoring their upcoming demos.
- We have full logs and a Mater Action Plan draft attached (MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_V2.pdf) for next steps: root-cause deep dive, longer-term fixes (connection robustness, adaptive server-side pacing), and SLA/credit discussion.

Proposed customer outcome
- Offer a one-off credit for the affected window (estimate: 5–10% of monthly invoice). Seeking approval to proceed.
- Schedule an executive call with VelociMed (Emma + CRO) tomorrow to review the RCA and our mitigation roadmap.

Request for Lauren / Leadership
- Approve the proposed customer credit and the exec call (preferred time: 2027-04-21 morning PT).
- Any guidance on public communications or additional concessions.

Thanks — we'll finalize the RCA and send the joint plan once we complete the deep dive.

-Aditya
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_V2.pdf, sr-12345-logs.txt]
